messages:
maya: Quick PR inbound to tweak pagination + streaming snippets: add resume example, note about opaque tokens, and a tiny jittered retry helper. PR: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/5123

sam: I'll update TS samples to use async iterator and include a 3-line jitter helper (no deps).

alex: I'll do Python. Will provide both async and sync snippets and a one-line file-persist example for cursors.

jia: Go examples from me: simple Recv loop + short resume pattern using ctx; will avoid external backoff libs.

sam: TS draft:

```ts
// stream (async iterator)
for await (const c of client.chat.stream({model:'redwood-1', input:'TL;DR'})) {
  process.stdout.write(c.delta ?? '')
}
// jittered retry (docs only)
async function retry(fn, tries=3){ for(let i=0;i<tries;i++){ try{return await fn()}catch(e){ if(i===tries-1) throw e; await new Promise(r=>setTimeout(r, Math.random()*100*(2**i))) } } }
```

alex: Python compact snippet:

```python
# async
async for m in client.chat.stream(model='redwood-1', input='Summarize'):
    print(m.text)
# sync fallback
for m in client.chat.stream_sync(model='redwood-1', input='Summarize'):
    print(m.text)
# persist cursor (one-liner)
open('/tmp/cursor','w').write(resp.next_cursor or '')
```

jia: Go recv loop + resume note:

```go
st, err := client.ChatStream(ctx, opts)
for { ch, err := st.Recv(); if err==io.EOF{break}; if err!=nil{log.Fatal(err)}; fmt.Print(ch.Delta) }
// resume: call List with resp.NextCursor and persist resp.NextCursor
```

maya: Add a one-line caveat in the pages: "pagination tokens are opaque and may be invalidated by model/quantization changes; resumed flows can produce duplicates so make operations idempotent."
